correctness.rationale: Direct expansion in u=e1+e3,v=e2+e3,w=e3 gives u²=0, uv=uw=vw=w²=u and v²=-u+λv. The quadratic map on the original natural basis forces exactly two isotropic lines Ku,K(w-u/2), and a nonzero-square line inside S=E² only when λ!=2. For planes containing Ku, closure forces S or T; otherwise intersection with S must be the extra line, and bilinear closure forces λ=4 and the sole plane P. All zero-, full-, characteristic-odd and exceptional-parameter branches are exhausted. The Boolean B3 case λ=4 and six-element order-ideal lattice λ=2 follow from concrete incidences; elsewhere the three line witness violates distributivity. Independent enumeration of every subspace over F3,F5,F7 at all λ!=0 reproduces 6/8/7 counts.
